newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DONATO DEALS PAIR OF DEUCES FOR VICTORY-STARVED BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DONATO DEALS PAIR OF DEUCES FOR VICTORY-STARVED BRUINS.

text.p: Ted Donato had two goals and two assists in a five-goal second period as the Boston Bruins broke a six-game winless skid Tuesday with a 6-4 win over the Penguins for their first victory in Pittsburgh in seven years.

Barry Richter and Tim Sweeney each had a goal and an assist and Adam Oates set up two scores for Boston, which had been 0-5-1 in their last six games. The Bruins ended an 0-12-1 drought in Pittsburgh, where they last won on January 2, 1990.
"It was needed, it's been a long time coming in here," Bruins coach Steve Kasper said.
Mario Lemieux converted a breakaway with 9:21 left in the second period for his second goal of the game and 17th of the season, pulling the Penguins within 4-2.

But Donato scored his first goal of the contest and seventh of the season 39 seconds later when he batted a rebound out of mid-air for a 5-2 lead. His second goal of the game with 6:26 to play in the period made it 6-2.
The Penguins have lost two in a row following a 10-game unbeaten streak.

At New York, Marty McInnis's power-play goal late in the second period snapped a tie and Bryan McCabe added an insurance goal with less than three minutes to go as the New York Islanders edged the Los Angeles Kings 4-3.
The win was New York's seventh in its last 11 games (7-3-1), but may be costly.

The Islanders lost right wing Zigmund Palffy -- who has a team-high 20 goals and 37 points -- with a sprained right shoulder suffered in a fight with Los Angeles' Kevin Stevens midway through the second period.
Kings' goaltender Stephane Fiset made 39 saves -- 19 in the first -- but fell to 5-11-3.

In Phoenix, Jim Johnson, Oleg Tverdovsky and Keith Tkachuk scored third-period goals and Darcy Wakaluk made 31 saves as the Phoenix Coyotes rallied for their third straight victory, 4-3 over the reeling Washington Capitals.

The Capitals, 0-6-1 in their last seven games, led 2-1 entering the third period, but Johnson tied it with his first goal of the season 2:54 into the period on a slap shot through a screen from the left point. Tverdovsky's goal gave Phoenix the lead for good with 9:37 remaining.
Wakaluk stopped all 12 shots in the third period until allowing Chris Simon's power-play goal with 18 seconds left. Wakaluk has won his last five decisions to improve to 7-1-1.

At Colorado, Scott Young and Eric Lacroix scored goals 3:19 apart in the third period to erase a one-goal deficit as the Colorado Avalanche ended the Detroit Red Wings' five-game unbeaten streak with a 4-3 victory.
Adam Deadmarsh, who assisted on both third-period goals, scored twice as the Avalanche improved to 11-3-3 at home.

With Detroit leading 3-2, Colorado had a two-man advantage. Young one-timed a pass from Joe Sakic between Mike Vernon's pads at 10:42 for his 11th goal. Colorado took the lead for good at 14:01 when Lacroix wristed in a rebound.
Patrick Roy made 30 saves and improved to 18-6-3.
In Hartford, Kevin Dineen scored the go-ahead goal with 7:17 to play as the Hartford Whalers defeated the St. Louis Blues 5-3 to snap a three-game losing streak.
Steven Rice scored twice for Hartford as St Louis lost for the third time in four games (0-3-1).
Jason Muzzatti, who was pulled after allowing three goals in just under nine minutes in Hartford's loss Monday to the New York Rangers, stopped 26 shots to earn the win.

In San Jose, Mats Sundin had two goals and an assist in the third period and Felix Potvin made 28 saves as the Toronto Maple Leafs ended a three-game losing streak with a 6-3 victory over the San Jose Sharks.

Sundin, who leads the team with 19 goals and 25 assists, drew an assist on Sergei Berezin's tie-breaking goal 32 seconds into the third period. He gave the Leafs a two-goal lead with an unassisted goal less than two minutes later and capped the scoring with a empty-netter with 45 seconds left.
Potvin made 10 saves in the first, eight in the second and 10 more in the third to post his 11th win of the season.
